newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales off 0.3 pct Sept -- Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales off 0.3 pct Sept -- Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales fell 0.3 percent in the first three weeks of fiscal September versus August, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 4.9 percent when compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 4.4 percent in the week ended September 21 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.

This was the softest week of the month so far, and below plan for most retailers, leading some to say they were scaling back their internal targets for the month, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.

"I think September is going to be very difficult to achieve plan on, although there are two more weeks -- it's a five week month this year -- so it can firm up; but I doubt it," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Looking forward, Eilenberg said October, November and December still look good for U.S. retailers because the comparisons against last year are easier.
"It was a tough fall last year and I think they should do well in those three months," he said.
Eilenberg also noted that retailers have had trouble in the home-goods department.
Appliances and home furnishings did very well the last few years, but they are not repeating robust sales this year, said Eilenberg.
